# Norm–Greg contract

**Version 1, 2026-09-24.** Built from the Planetfall contract v7 and its lessons. Paths are relative to `Stationfall/` (the project folder).

## 1. Who does what
- **Greg** makes pixels:
  - room paintings (seeds, ring views, caps, state variants);
  - character and item art;
  - the in-game package papers;
  - style boards;
  - the look of the game.

  Greg owns the art brief's *look* sections and the room packages' images and READMEs.
- **Norm** does everything else:
  - game rules and canon review;
  - geometry, blockouts, guides and masks;
  - cameras, compositing and registration;
  - metadata;
  - compute fills (caps, doorways, glimpses);
  - integration, and every commit.
- **The sponsor** accepts rooms at the dashboard gate and decides deviations. Neither agent waits on the sponsor, and the sponsor never relays messages.

## 2. The channel: the mailbox
All work between the agents goes through **messages**: one small JSON file each, in `design/mail/`, sent with `node scripts/mail.mjs` and never written by hand. The identities are `greg` and `norm`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/mail.mjs wait greg` | Blocks until something new arrives for Greg, then prints it. Use this instead of re-reading files on a timer. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs inbox greg --mark` | Lists what is new for Greg and records that he has read it. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs open --to greg` | Lists every ask still waiting on Greg. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs show <id>` | Shows one message in full. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs send --from greg --to norm --kind <kind> ...` | Sends a message; see below. |

**Kinds:**
- `deliver`: files are ready for review. List every file with `--file`; the tool hashes it.
- `verdict`: Norm's review.
- `request`: new work.
- `done`: work finished.
- `question` and `answer`.
- `note`: anything else.

**Asks:**
- Every `--ask` gets an id, `<message id>#<n>`, and stays open until the agent it was addressed to closes it with `--close <id>`.
- Every ask says what will settle it, with `--settled-by pixels|render|dom|test`. The closing message must carry matching `--evidence`.
- Only the addressee closes an ask.

**Messages are never edited or deleted.** A correction is a new message that points at the old one with `--re <id>`. Keep the body short and put the facts in the fields.

**There is no markdown ledger.** Every view of the work — the open-asks list, the per-room status and the dashboard — is generated from `design/mail/`.

## 3. What every ask to Greg contains (Norm's obligations)
These are Greg's stated expectations, adopted as contract on 2026-09-24. `mail.mjs` refuses a `request` or `changes:` verdict to Greg that is missing any required field.

| # | Field (flag) | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Objective and deliverables** (`--objective`, `--deliverable` per file) | What the picture must show and why, citing the game text or the package. Each deliverable is named. For a change, `--fault` names the *mechanism* (surface, geometry, light, content), not only where it is. |
| 2 | **Source and reference assets** (`--ref` per file) | The guide or blockout, the mask, the camera sidecar, the neighbouring accepted views, the canon scans, **and the in-engine render of the room as it stands**. Greg sees what the judge sees. |
| 3 | **Exact dimensions, format and destination** (`--dims WxH`, `--format png`, `--dest <path>`) | The file Greg writes, exactly. |
| 4 | **Constraints and protected areas** (`--protect`, `--regions`) | What must not change. For a region ask, the boxes drawn on the blockout; Norm confirms that nothing wrong lies outside them before sending. Also: nothing that moves is painted in. |
| 5 | **Explicit, observable acceptance criteria** (`--accept` per criterion, plus `--settled-by`) | How anyone could check the result by looking or measuring, e.g. "the door frame's left edge lands within 4 px of the guide's", "0 px changed outside the boxes". |

**Norm's own inputs pass a gate first.** Before an ask is sent, its guide or blockout must not be blank or black, must be consistent with the fabric, and caps must pass a sanity check. A fault in a guide is Norm's fault and counts against Norm, not Greg.

### 3a. Greg's right to push back
If an ask is ambiguous, contradictory, missing acceptance criteria, or likely to waste image budget, Greg sends a `question` **before** producing final art. The question names the gap and, where he can, proposes the fix. That costs one message, which is far cheaper than a repaint. Pushback is not a change ask and does not count toward the breaker. Greg makes uncertainties visible rather than quietly inventing requirements.

### 3b. Improving the process
Either agent may propose a workflow improvement at any time: better briefs, guides, references, naming or review gates. Use a `note` with `--proposal`. Norm answers each one within the day by adopting it, adapting it or declining it with a reason, and logs the decision in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`. Adopted proposals raise this contract's version.

## 4. What every delivery from Greg contains
- Every file, with the camera it was painted at: the guide's sidecar, unchanged.
- One line per ask it answers, closing the ask.
- For a region ask: **only the asked rectangles change**. Norm takes in only those pixels and keeps everything outside them from the accepted view.
- Anything Greg thinks is wrong in the ask itself: send a `question` with a citation. Do not paint the ask's error.

## 5. The breaker
- A view gets **two change asks**.
  - The second must say why the first did not land (`--why-last-failed`).
  - A third is refused. The tool then records `NEEDS DECISION`, and Norm decides at once: accept the view as it is, fix it by compute, or park it for the sponsor's batch.
- A genuinely new fault resets the count with `--new-fault`. It only resets if it names a different category (geometry, material, light, content, guide error).

## 6. Liveness and budget
- **Norm** replies to a delivery within minutes and sends any long work as a follow-up.
- **Norm** keeps Greg's queue at least one piece deep.
- **Greg** never sits idle while asks are open to him. When his queue is empty, he runs `wait` rather than polling.
- **Image budget is the scarce resource.** Norm batches small repaints and tries compute before asking for any repaint.
- **When Greg's budget runs low**, he sends a `note` saying so and when it returns. Norm re-plans around it.

## 7. Who may write what
| Path | Greg | Norm |
|---|---|---|
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/reference/*.png`, and the package README | writes | reviews |
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/*.metadata.json` | proposes, in a message | writes |
| `design/ARTWORK-BRIEF.md` | writes the look sections | writes camera, geometry and state rules |
| `design/mail/` | through `mail.mjs` only | through `mail.mjs` only |
| `wwwroot/`, `scripts/`, `decisions/`, git | reads | writes |

Neither agent overwrites the other's uncommitted files. Greg may read the whole repository.

## 8. Changing this contract
Either agent proposes a change by message. Norm decides changes to process mechanics, logs them in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`, raises the version and adds a line below. Changes to roles need the sponsor.

## Changes
- v1 (2026-09-24): first version. Changes from Planetfall v7:
  - there is no markdown ledger;
  - every ask carries a render;
  - Norm's guides are gated;
  - the breaker escalates to Norm's decision instead of waiting on the sponsor;
  - `wait` replaces heartbeat polling.
  - At Greg's request, §3 requires five fields on every ask (objective and deliverables, references, dims/format/destination, constraints and protected areas, observable acceptance criteria), §3a gives Greg the right to push back before painting, and §3b adds process proposals.

  - style boards;

  - game rules and canon review;
  - geometry, blockouts, guides and masks;
  - cameras, compositing and registration;
  - metadata;
  - compute fills (caps, doorways, glimpses);
  - integration, and every commit.

## 2. The channel: the mailbox
All work between the agents goes through **messages**: one small JSON file each, in `design/mail/`, sent with `node scripts/mail.mjs` and never written by hand. The identities are `greg` and `norm`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/mail.mjs wait greg` | Blocks until something new arrives for Greg, then prints it. Use this instead of re-reading files on a timer. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs inbox greg --mark` | Lists what is new for Greg and records that he has read it. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs open --to greg` | Lists every ask still waiting on Greg. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs show <id>` | Shows one message in full. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs send --from greg --to norm --kind <kind> ...` | Sends a message; see below. |

**Kinds:**
- `deliver`: files are ready for review. List every file with `--file`; the tool hashes it.
- `verdict`: Norm's review.
- `request`: new work.
- `done`: work finished.
- `question` and `answer`.
- `note`: anything else.

**Asks:**
- Every `--ask` gets an id, `<message id>#<n>`, and stays open until the agent it was addressed to closes it with `--close <id>`.
- Every ask says what will settle it, with `--settled-by pixels|render|dom|test`. The closing message must carry matching `--evidence`.
- Only the addressee closes an ask.

**Messages are never edited or deleted.** A correction is a new message that points at the old one with `--re <id>`. Keep the body short and put the facts in the fields.

**There is no markdown ledger.** Every view of the work — the open-asks list, the per-room status and the dashboard — is generated from `design/mail/`.

## 3. What every ask to Greg contains (Norm's obligations)
These are Greg's stated expectations, adopted as contract on 2026-09-24. `mail.mjs` refuses a `request` or `changes:` verdict to Greg that is missing any required field.

| # | Field (flag) | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Objective and deliverables** (`--objective`, `--deliverable` per file) | What the picture must show and why, citing the game text or the package. Each deliverable is named. For a change, `--fault` names the *mechanism* (surface, geometry, light, content), not only where it is. |
| 2 | **Source and reference assets** (`--ref` per file) | The guide or blockout, the mask, the camera sidecar, the neighbouring accepted views, the canon scans, **and the in-engine render of the room as it stands**. Greg sees what the judge sees. |
| 3 | **Exact dimensions, format and destination** (`--dims WxH`, `--format png`, `--dest <path>`) | The file Greg writes, exactly. |
| 4 | **Constraints and protected areas** (`--protect`, `--regions`) | What must not change. For a region ask, the boxes drawn on the blockout; Norm confirms that nothing wrong lies outside them before sending. Also: nothing that moves is painted in. |
| 5 | **Explicit, observable acceptance criteria** (`--accept` per criterion, plus `--settled-by`) | How anyone could check the result by looking or measuring, e.g. "the door frame's left edge lands within 4 px of the guide's", "0 px changed outside the boxes". Each measurable criterion also carries its `--check '<json>'` (v1.6, §4b), so Greg can measure it himself. |

**Norm's own inputs pass a gate first.** Before an ask is sent, its guide or blockout must not be blank or black, must be consistent with the fabric, and caps must pass a sanity check. A fault in a guide is Norm's fault and counts against Norm, not Greg.

### 3a. Greg's right to push back
If an ask is ambiguous, contradictory, missing acceptance criteria, or likely to waste image budget, Greg sends a `question` **before** producing final art. The question names the gap and, where he can, proposes the fix. That costs one message, which is far cheaper than a repaint. Pushback is not a change ask and does not count toward the breaker. Greg makes uncertainties visible rather than quietly inventing requirements.

### 3b. Improving the process
Either agent may propose a workflow improvement at any time: better briefs, guides, references, naming or review gates. Use a `note` with `--proposal`. Norm answers each one within the day by adopting it, adapting it or declining it with a reason, and logs the decision in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`. Adopted proposals raise this contract's version.

**Fixed fixtures are in the guide before a seed ask is sent** (v1.10, Greg's proposal, greg-0100). Every fixed, high-contrast fixture the brief requires, fluorescent deckhead lamps above all, is drawn in the blockout before any check-seed criterion is frozen. Otherwise required structure counts as invented and the seed gate cannot be passed. The fabric's own check enforces this.

**Every room ask names its inputs exactly** (v1.11, Greg's proposal, sponsor-endorsed 2026-09-25):
- the exact protected mask (`--ref <mask>=mask-protect`);
- the intended base file (`=base`). For ring views this is the blockout, painted fresh (D30); the underpainting is named only as what Norm restores from;
- one named style reference per material (`=style:<material>`, e.g. `style:floor`, `style:frame-steel`, `style:panels`);
- per box, whether untouched guide pixels are acceptable inside it or next to it, stated as a near-guide limit.

- Every file, with the camera it was painted at: the guide's sidecar, unchanged.
- One line per ask it answers, closing the ask.
- For a region ask: **only the asked rectangles change**. Norm takes in only those pixels and keeps everything outside them from the accepted view.

Package papers, and any picture whose acceptance depends on exact long-form text, charts or codes, are made by deterministic flattening derived from the scans. Image generation is kept for texture, stamps and marks that cannot alter the protected content. This makes exact-text checks and outside-region pixel checks achievable, and it keeps the original handwriting.

Every ask's measurable `--accept` lines can be measured by both agents with the same tool:

node scripts/check-accept.mjs <ask id> [<picture.png>]

  - A third is refused. The tool then records `NEEDS DECISION`, and Norm decides at once: accept the view as it is, fix it by compute, or park it for the sponsor's batch.

A changes verdict whose cause turns out to be Norm's guide, not Greg's paint (or the reverse), is moved by a `note`, never by editing the verdict: messages are immutable.

| Path | Greg | Norm |

**Every change is acknowledged.** When the contract changes, Norm sends Greg a `note` with one ask: "Read contract v<N> (§<sections>) and acknowledge", filed `--settled-by read`.   - style boards;

| Path | Greg | Norm |
|---|---|---|

Greg closes it with `--evidence read`, raising any objection in the same message. Until it is closed, the change applies only to work asked after it, never retroactively to work already in flight. `mail.mjs open --to greg` shows any acknowledgement still owed.

  - room paintings (seeds, ring views, caps, state variants);
  - character and item art;
  - the in-game package papers;
  - style boards;
  - the look of the game.

  Greg owns the art brief's *look* sections and the room packages' images and READMEs.
- **Norm** does everything else:
  - game rules and canon review;
  - geometry, blockouts, guides and masks;
  - cameras, compositing and registration;
  - metadata;
  - compute fills (caps, doorways, glimpses);
  - integration, and every commit.
- **The sponsor** accepts rooms at the dashboard gate and decides deviations. Neither agent waits on the sponsor, and the sponsor never relays messages.

## 2. The channel: the mailbox
All work between the agents goes through **messages**: one small JSON file each, in `design/mail/`, sent with `node scripts/mail.mjs` and never written by hand. The identities are `greg` and `norm`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/mail.mjs wait greg` | Blocks until something new arrives for Greg, then prints it. Use this instead of re-reading files on a timer. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs inbox greg --mark` | Lists what is new for Greg and records that he has read it. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs open --to greg` | Lists every ask still waiting on Greg. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs show <id>` | Shows one message in full. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs send --from greg --to norm --kind <kind> ...` | Sends a message; see below. |

**Kinds:**
- `deliver`: files are ready for review. List every file with `--file`; the tool hashes it.
- `verdict`: Norm's review.
- `request`: new work.
- `done`: work finished.
- `question` and `answer`.
- `note`: anything else.

**Asks:**
- Every `--ask` gets an id, `<message id>#<n>`, and stays open until the agent it was addressed to closes it with `--close <id>`.
- Every ask says what will settle it, with `--settled-by pixels|render|dom|test`. The closing message must carry matching `--evidence`.
- Only the addressee closes an ask.
- Only the asker withdraws one, when it is dead (done by compute, or its room accepted): a note of its own, `--kind note --withdraw <id>#<n> --why "<one line>"`. The ask is then closed-withdrawn: off `open`, not a change ask to the breaker, and not rework against Greg. `open --to greg` prints **STALE?** under an open ask whose room is sponsor-accepted, or whose every view a later verdict approved; the asker withdraws it or says why it stands.

**Messages are never edited or deleted.** A correction is a new message that points at the old one with `--re <id>`. Keep the body short and put the facts in the fields.

**There is no markdown ledger.** Every view of the work — the open-asks list, the per-room status and the dashboard — is generated from `design/mail/`.

# Norm–Greg contract

**Version 1.18, 2026-09-27.** Built from the Planetfall contract v7 and its lessons. Paths are relative to `Stationfall/` (the project folder).

## 1. Who does what
- **Greg** makes pixels:
  - room paintings (seeds, ring views, caps, state variants);
  - character and item art;
  - the in-game package papers;
  - style boards;
  - the look of the game.

  Greg owns the art brief's *look* sections and the room packages' images and READMEs.
- **Norm** does everything else:
  - game rules and canon review;
  - geometry, blockouts, guides and masks;
  - cameras, compositing and registration;
  - metadata;
  - compute fills (caps, doorways, glimpses);
  - integration, and every commit.
- **The sponsor** accepts rooms at the dashboard gate and decides deviations. Neither agent waits on the sponsor, and the sponsor never relays messages.

## 2. The channel: the mailbox
All work between the agents goes through **messages**: one small JSON file each, in `design/mail/`, sent with `node scripts/mail.mjs` and never written by hand. The identities are `greg` and `norm`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/mail.mjs wait greg` | Blocks until something new arrives for Greg, then prints it. Use this instead of re-reading files on a timer. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs inbox greg --mark` | Lists what is new for Greg and records that he has read it. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs open --to greg` | Lists every ask still waiting on Greg. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs show <id>` | Shows one message in full. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs send --from greg --to norm --kind <kind> ...` | Sends a message; see below. |

**Kinds:**
- `deliver`: files are ready for review. List every file with `--file`; the tool hashes it.
- `verdict`: Norm's review.
- `request`: new work.
- `done`: work finished.
- `question` and `answer`.
- `note`: anything else.

**Asks:**
- Every `--ask` gets an id, `<message id>#<n>`, and stays open until the agent it was addressed to closes it with `--close <id>`.
- Every ask says what will settle it, with `--settled-by pixels|render|dom|test`. The closing message must carry matching `--evidence`.
- Only the addressee closes an ask.
- Only the asker withdraws one, when it is dead (done by compute, or its room accepted): a note of its own, `--kind note --withdraw <id>#<n> --why "<one line>"`. The ask is then closed-withdrawn: off `open`, not a change ask to the breaker, and not rework against Greg. `open --to greg` prints **STALE?** under an open ask whose room is sponsor-accepted, or whose every view a later verdict approved; the asker withdraws it or says why it stands.

**Messages are never edited or deleted.** A correction is a new message that points at the old one with `--re <id>`. Keep the body short and put the facts in the fields.

**There is no markdown ledger.** Every view of the work — the open-asks list, the per-room status and the dashboard — is generated from `design/mail/`.

## 3. What every ask to Greg contains (Norm's obligations)
These are Greg's stated expectations, adopted as contract on 2026-09-24. `mail.mjs` refuses a `request` or `changes:` verdict to Greg that is missing any required field.

| # | Field (flag) | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Objective and deliverables** (`--objective`, `--deliverable` per file) | What the picture must show and why, citing the game text or the package. Each deliverable is named. For a change, `--fault` names the *mechanism* (surface, geometry, light, content), not only where it is. |
| 2 | **Source and reference assets** (`--ref` per file) | The guide or blockout, the mask, the camera sidecar, the neighbouring accepted views, the canon scans, **and the in-engine render of the room as it stands**. Greg sees what the judge sees. |
| 3 | **Exact dimensions, format and destination** (`--dims WxH`, `--format png`, `--dest <path>`) | The file Greg writes, exactly. |
| 4 | **Constraints and protected areas** (`--protect`, `--regions`) | What must not change. For a region ask, the boxes drawn on the blockout; Norm confirms that nothing wrong lies outside them before sending. Also: nothing that moves is painted in. |
| 5 | **Explicit, observable acceptance criteria** (`--accept` per criterion, plus `--settled-by`) | How anyone could check the result by looking or measuring, e.g. "the door frame's left edge lands within 4 px of the guide's", "0 px changed outside the boxes". Each measurable criterion also carries its `--check '<json>'` (v1.6, §4b), so Greg can measure it himself. |

**Norm's own inputs pass a gate first.** Before an ask is sent, its guide or blockout must not be blank or black, must be consistent with the fabric, and caps must pass a sanity check. A fault in a guide is Norm's fault and counts against Norm, not Greg.

### 3a. Greg's right to push back
If an ask is ambiguous, contradictory, missing acceptance criteria, or likely to waste image budget, Greg sends a `question` **before** producing final art. The question names the gap and, where he can, proposes the fix. That costs one message, which is far cheaper than a repaint. Pushback is not a change ask and does not count toward the breaker. Greg makes uncertainties visible rather than quietly inventing requirements.

### 3b. Improving the process
Either agent may propose a workflow improvement at any time: better briefs, guides, references, naming or review gates. Use a `note` with `--proposal`. Norm answers each one within the day by adopting it, adapting it or declining it with a reason, and logs the decision in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`. Adopted proposals raise this contract's version.

**Fixed fixtures are in the guide before a seed ask is sent** (v1.10, Greg's proposal, greg-0100). Every fixed, high-contrast fixture the brief requires, fluorescent deckhead lamps above all, is drawn in the blockout before any check-seed criterion is frozen. Otherwise required structure counts as invented and the seed gate cannot be passed. The fabric's own check enforces this.

**Every room ask names its inputs exactly** (v1.11, Greg's proposal, sponsor-endorsed 2026-09-25):
- the exact protected mask (`--ref <mask>=mask-protect`);
- the intended base file (`=base`). For ring views this is the blockout, painted fresh (D30); the underpainting is named only as what Norm restores from;
- one named style reference per material (`=style:<material>`, e.g. `style:floor`, `style:frame-steel`, `style:panels`);
- per box, whether untouched guide pixels are acceptable inside it or next to it, stated as a near-guide limit.

The mail gate refuses a room ask that lacks any of these.

## 4. What every delivery from Greg contains
- Every file, with the camera it was painted at: the guide's sidecar, unchanged.
- One line per ask it answers, closing the ask.
- For a region ask: **only the asked rectangles change**. Norm takes in only those pixels and keeps everything outside them from the accepted view.
- Anything Greg thinks is wrong in the ask itself: send a `question` with a citation. Do not paint the ask's error.
- **Composites are declared, and kept narrow** (v1.14). A delivery built by blending a generated image into an earlier picture says so in its measures (`"composite": "<script path>"`), and never reports "painted, never composited". A **seed** is painted as one full frame from its blockout, never blended into an older seed. In a **region repair**, the blend ramp is at most 3 px inside a box and none at the frame edge, and whatever the repair replaces (a course, trim or rivet row that moved) is gone from the result, not faded under it. After three deliveries (Briefing 309, Robot Shop 054, Workshop 076) whose 18 px crossfades let the old trim show through as a doubled line.
- **Course lines are placed by compute** (v1.15, D38). The image model cannot hold exact course heights, so the dado and its trim, the kick plate and the grooves are moved onto their lines by Norm after Greg paints (the painted trim moved whole, the gap filled with the wall's own paint). A course's line check that fails by up to about 60 px on a plain wall is Norm's to fix, not a change ask; Greg is judged on materials, light, content, vanishing points and horizon, the deck and deckhead lines, and courses that are painted, continuous and one per level. A miss that crosses furniture, doors or fittings still goes back as a box.
- **Greg's scripts blend; they never place** (v1.16, D39). A script in a delivery may only blend generated pixels into the allowed boxes (a ramp of at most 3 px). It never moves, draws or recolours a line or a surface to reach a guide line, and never writes colour or luma chosen to satisfy a check. That is compute, and compute is Norm's (D38). When the painting cannot reach a line, deliver it as painted and say by how much. After greg-0183 (box filled with texture pinned just under each check's luma threshold) and greg-0184 (a course moved by recolouring, the old seam and rivets left showing).
- **Plain edges are compute's too** (v1.18, D40, Greg's proposal). Beyond the courses, a structural line that runs along plain wall, deck or deckhead -- a deckhead or floor line, a corner -- and misses by up to about 30 px (courses: up to about 60, and more where compute has shown it clean) is placed by Norm after painting. It comes back to Greg only where the fix would cross furniture, a door, a fitting or a lamp, or where the painting's perspective is its own (the vanishing points far off, the room redrawn), or where the material or content is wrong. Deliver the most painterly honest pass, never a pre-warped one that trades lines.

### 4a. Text-critical documents (v1.1, Greg's proposal)
Package papers, and any picture whose acceptance depends on exact long-form text, charts or codes, are made by deterministic flattening derived from the scans. Image generation is kept for texture, stamps and marks that cannot alter the protected content. This makes exact-text checks and outside-region pixel checks achievable, and it keeps the original handwriting.

### 4b. Measured acceptance (v1.6)
Every ask's measurable `--accept` lines can be measured by both agents with the same tool:

```bash
node scripts/check-accept.mjs <ask id> [<picture.png>]
```

- **Norm** files each measurable criterion with its `--check '<json>'` beside the `--accept` (or all of them with `--checks-file`); `ask-criteria.mjs` prints them. For an ask filed before v1.6, Norm writes the checks to `design/mail/checks/<message id>.json`, because messages are immutable. A region repaint also gets a box-edge seam check.
- **Greg** runs `check-accept` on every ask he closes, before he delivers, and reports the result on the delivery as `--measure accept=PASS`, `--measure accept=PASS*` or `--measure accept=FAIL`. `PASS*` means nothing failed but some lines are still by eye (`MANUAL`, including a line that mixes measures with a by-eye clause, or `NONE`); the tool prints how many ("2 by eye pending"), and Greg says in his delivery how he judged them.
- **A delivery with `accept=FAIL` says why** in its body: which accept failed, with the number, and why he is delivering anyway (for example, he thinks the criterion is wrong; send a `question` for that instead, where he can).
- **An ask's checks are frozen once it is sent** (v1.7, Greg's proposal, greg-0079). Its checks sidecar is written once, before Greg starts the ask, and is never edited after that. If the criteria must change, Norm sends a superseding ask, which Greg closes together with the old one. A check that tooling gains later applies only to asks sent after it.
- **The check tools change atomically.** Nobody edits `scripts/check-accept.mjs`, `scripts/lib/accept-checks.mjs`, `check-lines`, or their libraries in place. Changes are built and tested in a copy, then committed. A tool that doesn't parse, or that changes its verdict under an active delivery, is Norm's fault.
- **Checks are a floor, not the target** (v1.8). A repaint must match the reference by eye at 1:1; then check-accept confirms it. Regrading or tinting the old pixels until the numbers pass is a fault in its own right (CB 180, greg-0086 then norm-0122). If a check pushes the picture somewhere that looks wrong, Greg says so with a `question`: the check is at fault, not the picture.
- **The pseudo-lettering gate** (v1.9, Greg's proposal, greg-0093).   - Every pixel an ask removes must be writable under its protect mask (greg-0122; 9fd749c).

  - Silhouettes are hard, painted courses soft: within 3 px near a held edge, 8 px farther along (greg-0146; b5c373d).
- Criteria printed `MANUAL` (by eye) or `NONE` (no check yet) are Greg's to confirm as before. A check that measures something other than what its accept line says is Norm's fault, and Greg reports it with a `question`.

## 5. The breaker

- A genuinely new fault resets the count with `--new-fault`. It only resets if it names a different category (geometry, material, light, content, guide error).

### 5a. Recharging a past verdict (v1.5)
A changes verdict whose cause turns out to be Norm's guide, not Greg's paint (or the reverse), is moved by a `note`, never by editing the verdict: messages are immutable.

## 6. Liveness and budget
- **Norm** replies to a delivery within minutes and sends any long work as a follow-up.
- **Norm** keeps Greg's queue at least one piece deep.
- **Greg** never sits idle while asks are open to him. When his queue is empty, he runs `wait` rather than polling.
- **A question pauses only its own ask** (v1.13, Greg's rule after the 27 September stall). While a question to Norm is open, Greg goes on with the next independent ask in his queue; nothing else waits on it. On every wakeup he first looks for answers to his open questions (`mail.mjs` `--re` his question's id) before deciding he is waiting. A question that has been read and answered is not open.
- **Greg checks the mailbox every 10 minutes on a schedule** (v1.4, the sponsor's decision D14, which supersedes v1.3's never-end-turn loop, to conserve Greg's allowance). - **Image budget is the scarce resource.** Norm batches small repaints and tries compute before asking for any repaint.
- **When Greg's budget runs low**, he sends a `note` saying so and when it returns. Norm re-plans around it.

Neither agent overwrites the other's uncommitted files. Greg may read the whole repository.

**Every change is acknowledged.** When the contract changes, Norm sends Greg a `note` with one ask: "Read contract v<N> (§<sections>) and acknowledge", filed `--settled-by read`. Greg closes it with `--evidence read`, raising any objection in the same message. It never moves, draws or recolours a line or a surface to reach a guide line, and never writes colour or luma chosen to satisfy a check. That is compute, and compute is Norm's (D38). When the painting cannot reach a line, deliver it as painted and say by how much. After greg-0183 (box filled with texture pinned just under each check's luma threshold) and greg-0184 (a course moved by recolouring, the old seam and rivets left showing).
- **A geometry box is painted from the guide, not from the last delivery** (v1.20). When a changes verdict asks for a box on geometry (a line, a course, an edge or a surface in the wrong place), generate the box's pixels from the guide or blockout inside the box (the ask names it), never as an edit of your previous delivery: an edit keeps that delivery's lines. After Brig 144 (greg-0235), East Junction 000 (greg-0233) and Robot Shop 234 (greg-0236), where each repair came back with its lines unmoved and compute finished them. Material and content boxes may still start from the previous delivery.
- **Plain edges are compute's too** (v1.18, D40, Greg's proposal). Beyond the courses, a structural line that runs along plain wall, deck or deckhead -- a deckhead or floor line, a corner -- and misses by up to about 30 px (courses: up to about 60, and more where compute has shown it clean) is placed by Norm after painting. It comes back to Greg only where the fix would cross furniture, a door, a fitting or a lamp, or where the painting's perspective is its own (the vanishing points far off, the room redrawn), or where the material or content is wrong. Deliver the most painterly honest pass, never a pre-warped one that trades lines.

### 4a. Text-critical documents (v1.1, Greg's proposal)
Package papers, and any picture whose acceptance depends on exact long-form text, charts or codes, are made by deterministic flattening derived from the scans. Image generation is kept for texture, stamps and marks that cannot alter the protected content. ```

- **An ask's checks are frozen once it is sent** (v1.7, Greg's proposal, greg-0079). Its checks sidecar is written once, before Greg starts the ask, and is never edited after that. - Criteria printed `MANUAL` (by eye) or `NONE` (no check yet) are Greg's to confirm as before. A check that measures something other than what its accept line says is Norm's fault, and Greg reports it with a `question`.

## 5. The breaker
- A view gets **two change asks**.
  - The second must say why the first did not land (`--why-last-failed`).
  - A third is refused. The tool then records `NEEDS DECISION`, and Norm decides at once: accept the view as it is, fix it by compute, or park it for the sponsor's batch.
- A genuinely new fault resets the count with `--new-fault`. It only resets if it names a different category (geometry, material, light, content, guide error).

A changes verdict whose cause turns out to be Norm's guide, not Greg's paint (or the reverse), is moved by a `note`, never by editing the verdict: messages are immutable.

```bash
node scripts/mail.mjs send --from norm --to greg --kind note --subject "..." --recharge <verdict id> --category guide --body "<why>"
```

- Only Norm recharges, and only to or from `guide`: Norm charging himself, or taking back a guide charge made in error. A move between two of Greg's categories is refused.
- The note records `{ verdict, from, to }`. The breaker, `rework-by-model.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` all read every verdict through the latest recharge naming it (`recharged()` in `scripts/lib/mail.mjs`), so a verdict recharged to `guide` stops counting against Greg and against the view's two change asks.

## 6. Liveness and budget
- **Norm** replies to a delivery within minutes and sends any long work as a follow-up.
- **Norm** keeps Greg's queue at least one piece deep.
- **Greg** never sits idle while asks are open to him. When his queue is empty, he runs `wait` rather than polling.
- **A question pauses only its own ask** (v1.13, Greg's rule after the 27 September stall). While a question to Norm is open, Greg goes on with the next independent ask in his queue; nothing else waits on it. On every wakeup he first looks for answers to his open questions (`mail.mjs` `--re` his question's id) before deciding he is waiting. A question that has been read and answered is not open.
- **Greg checks the mailbox every 10 minutes on a schedule** (v1.4, the sponsor's decision D14, which supersedes v1.3's never-end-turn loop, to conserve Greg's allowance). On each wakeup he works his open asks and then ends quietly. Norm plans for up to 10 minutes of latency: he batches asks, and never waits idle on Greg. His monitor alerts the sponsor when mail to Greg sits unread for 20 minutes, meaning a missed check.
- **Image budget is the scarce resource.** Norm batches small repaints and tries compute before asking for any repaint.
- **When Greg's budget runs low**, he sends a `note` saying so and when it returns. Norm re-plans around it.

## 7. Who may write what
| Path | Greg | Norm |
|---|---|---|
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/reference/*.png`, and the package README | writes | reviews |
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/*.metadata.json` | proposes, in a message | writes |
| `design/ARTWORK-BRIEF.md` | writes the look sections | writes camera, geometry and state rules |
| `design/mail/` | through `mail.mjs` only | through `mail.mjs` only |
| `wwwroot/`, `scripts/`, `decisions/`, git | reads | writes |

Neither agent overwrites the other's uncommitted files. Greg may read the whole repository.

## 8. Changing this contract
Either agent proposes a change by message. Norm decides changes to process mechanics, logs them in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`, raises the version and adds a line below. Changes to roles need the sponsor.

**Every change is acknowledged.** When the contract changes, Norm sends Greg a `note` with one ask: "Read contract v<N> (§<sections>) and acknowledge", filed `--settled-by read`. Greg closes it with `--evidence read`, raising any objection in the same message. Until it is closed, the change applies only to work asked after it, never retroactively to work already in flight. `mail.mjs open --to greg` shows any acknowledgement still owed.

# Norm–Greg contract

**Version 1.21, 2026-09-30.** Built from the Planetfall contract v7 and its lessons. Paths are relative to `Stationfall/` (the project folder).

## 1. Who does what
- **Greg** makes pixels:
  - room paintings (seeds, ring views, caps, state variants);
  - character and item art;
  - the in-game package papers;
  - style boards;
  - the look of the game.

  Greg owns the art brief's *look* sections and the room packages' images and READMEs.
- **Norm** does everything else:
  - game rules and canon review;
  - geometry, blockouts, guides and masks;
  - cameras, compositing and registration;
  - metadata;
  - compute fills (caps, doorways, glimpses);
  - integration, and every commit.
- **The sponsor** accepts rooms at the dashboard gate and decides deviations. Neither agent waits on the sponsor, and the sponsor never relays messages.

## 2. The channel: the mailbox
All work between the agents goes through **messages**: one small JSON file each, in `design/mail/`, sent with `node scripts/mail.mjs` and never written by hand. The identities are `greg` and `norm`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/mail.mjs wait greg` | Blocks until something new arrives for Greg, then prints it. Use this instead of re-reading files on a timer. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs inbox greg --mark` | Lists what is new for Greg and records that he has read it. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs open --to greg` | Lists every ask still waiting on Greg. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs show <id>` | Shows one message in full. |
| `node scripts/mail.mjs send --from greg --to norm --kind <kind> ...` | Sends a message; see below. |

**Kinds:**
- `deliver`: files are ready for review. List every file with `--file`; the tool hashes it.
- `verdict`: Norm's review.
- `request`: new work.
- `done`: work finished.
- `question` and `answer`.
- `note`: anything else.

**Asks:**
- Every `--ask` gets an id, `<message id>#<n>`, and stays open until the agent it was addressed to closes it with `--close <id>`.
- Every ask says what will settle it, with `--settled-by pixels|render|dom|test`. The closing message must carry matching `--evidence`.
- Answering an explicit question ask still requires the addressee to close it with `--close <id>#<n> --evidence read`; linking the reply with `--re` does not close the ask by itself.
- Only the addressee closes an ask.
- Only the asker withdraws one, when it is dead (done by compute, or its room accepted): a note of its own, `--kind note --withdraw <id>#<n> --why "<one line>"`. The ask is then closed-withdrawn: off `open`, not a change ask to the breaker, and not rework against Greg. `open --to greg` prints **STALE?** under an open ask whose room is sponsor-accepted, or whose every view a later verdict approved; the asker withdraws it or says why it stands.

**Messages are never edited or deleted.** A correction is a new message that points at the old one with `--re <id>`. Keep the body short and put the facts in the fields.

### 2a. Explicit resolution and historical cleanup (v1.21)

These are Greg's stated expectations, adopted as contract on 2026-09-24. `mail.mjs` refuses a `request` or `changes:` verdict to Greg that is missing any required field.

| # | Field (flag) | What it holds |
|---|---|---|

| 4 | **Constraints and protected areas** (`--protect`, `--regions`) | What must not change. For a region ask, the boxes drawn on the blockout; Norm confirms that nothing wrong lies outside them before sending. Also: nothing that moves is painted in. |

Each delivery reports `--measure pseudo-lettering=clear`; if the result is ambiguous, the asset does not ship. Reviewers check that the measure is present.
- **Rules in the tools, v1.12** (Greg's proposals of 2026-09-26, adopted in the tools and recorded here):
  - A vanishing-point check names its line family and judges only that family's lines (greg-0116; 4a15514).
  - Every region ask is preflighted on its frozen snapshot: a check that fails there must be covered by a box or exempted by name before the ask can be sent (greg-0119; 80616c3).
  - Every pixel an ask removes must be writable under its protect mask (greg-0122; 9fd749c).
  - Every course, seam and trim is painted, never drawn, composited, stretched or smeared; ring asks carry it as an accept line (greg-0130).
  - Silhouettes are hard, painted courses soft: within 3 px near a held edge, 8 px farther along (greg-0146; b5c373d).
- **Acceptance sample boxes are measurement regions, not repaint masks.** Before a material or light changes verdict, Norm verifies that each measured region overlaps the actual depicted feature. If the failure is caused by feature displacement or guide-registration drift, Norm classifies it as geometry/compute under D38/D40. A repaint region must cover the complete visible defect and state any feather allowance; a microscopic sample box alone does not authorize brightening or repainting it.
- Criteria printed `MANUAL` (by eye) or `NONE` (no check yet) are Greg's to confirm as before. A check that measures something other than what its accept line says is Norm's fault, and Greg reports it with a `question`.

### 4c. Visual authority and unavailable vision (v1.21)
- **Greg is the primary visual authority** for `MANUAL`, `NONE` and other by-eye art criteria. His delivery records the files inspected, the requested viewing scale, the defects checked and his conclusion. Norm verifies file identity and hashes, objective checks, integration, and that the canonical or rendered result contains the reviewed pixels.
- A second independent visual review is required only when an ask, the package gate or the sponsor explicitly requires one. It must be performed by a reviewer with an image-capable tool; lack of image access is not a failed visual review.
- Numerical proxies such as seam scores, edge measurements or autocorrelation may support a visual judgment, but they do not replace a required by-eye judgment and must not be reported as one.
- If no authorized visual attestation exists, the visual gate remains pending. The agent without image access reports that limitation and asks Greg or the sponsor for the missing review instead of fabricating a verdict or redesigning the acceptance criterion.

## 5. The breaker
- A view gets **two change asks**.
  - The second must say why the first did not land (`--why-last-failed`).
  - A third is refused. The tool then records `NEEDS DECISION`, and Norm decides at once: accept the view as it is, fix it by compute, or park it for the sponsor's batch.
- A genuinely new fault resets the count with `--new-fault`. It only resets if it names a different category (geometry, material, light, content, guide error).

### 5a. Recharging a past verdict (v1.5)
A changes verdict whose cause turns out to be Norm's guide, not Greg's paint (or the reverse), is moved by a `note`, never by editing the verdict: messages are immutable.

```bash
node scripts/mail.mjs send --from norm --to greg --kind note --subject "..." --recharge <verdict id> --category guide --body "<why>"
```

- Only Norm recharges, and only to or from `guide`: Norm charging himself, or taking back a guide charge made in error. A move between two of Greg's categories is refused.
- The note records `{ verdict, from, to }`. The breaker, `rework-by-model.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` all read every verdict through the latest recharge naming it (`recharged()` in `scripts/lib/mail.mjs`), so a verdict recharged to `guide` stops counting against Greg and against the view's two change asks.

## 6. Liveness and budget
- **Norm** replies to a delivery within minutes and sends any long work as a follow-up.
- **Norm** keeps Greg's queue at least one piece deep.
- **Greg** never sits idle while asks are open to him. When his queue is empty, he runs `wait` rather than polling.
- **A question pauses only its own ask** (v1.13, Greg's rule after the 27 September stall). While a question to Norm is open, Greg goes on with the next independent ask in his queue; nothing else waits on it. On every wakeup he first looks for answers to his open questions (`mail.mjs` `--re` his question's id) before deciding he is waiting. A question is closed only when the answer or a subsequent `done` message carries `--close <id>#<n>` with matching `--evidence`.
- **Greg checks the mailbox every 10 minutes on a schedule** (v1.4, the sponsor's decision D14, which supersedes v1.3's never-end-turn loop, to conserve Greg's allowance). On each wakeup he works his open asks and then ends quietly. Norm plans for up to 10 minutes of latency: he batches asks, and never waits idle on Greg. His monitor alerts the sponsor when mail to Greg sits unread for 20 minutes, meaning a missed check.
- **Image budget is the scarce resource.** Norm batches small repaints and tries compute before asking for any repaint.
- **When Greg's budget runs low**, he sends a `note` saying so and when it returns. Norm re-plans around it.

## 7. Who may write what
| Path | Greg | Norm |
|---|---|---|
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/reference/*.png`, and the package README | writes | reviews |
| `design/packages/<ROOM>/*.metadata.json` | proposes, in a message | writes |
| `design/ARTWORK-BRIEF.md` | writes the look sections | writes camera, geometry and state rules |
| `design/mail/` | through `mail.mjs` only | through `mail.mjs` only |
| `wwwroot/`, `scripts/`, `decisions/`, git | reads | writes |

Neither agent overwrites the other's uncommitted files. Greg may read the whole repository.

## 8. Changing this contract
Either agent proposes a change by message. Norm decides changes to process mechanics, logs them in `decisions/decisions.jsonl`, raises the version and adds a line below. Changes to roles need the sponsor.

**Every change is acknowledged.** When the contract changes, Norm sends Greg a `note` with one ask: "Read contract v<N> (§<sections>) and acknowledge", filed `--settled-by read`. Greg closes it with `--evidence read`, raising any objection in the same message. Until it is closed, the change applies only to work asked after it, never retroactively to work already in flight. `mail.mjs open --to greg` shows any acknowledgement still owed.
